name: Release 1: Meshwright release tooling (Modelfiles, GGUF tag rows, preflight, ops, v2 runbook, release gate)
description: Offline tooling for docs/15-release.md. Meshwright v1 is already published (HF private, Ollama public). This PRD makes the next steps repeatable and checkable: (1) generate Modelfiles from the frozen prompt instead of hand-editing them, (2) model rows for the v1 and v1-gguf Ollama tags, including a no-system-message mode that matches what an Ollama user sends, (3) a preflight check before anything goes public, (4) an owner-session ops script for the v1-gguf dev-brief gate, (5) a dry-run-first v2 pod runbook that refuses to spend without explicit flags, (6) a v1-versus-v2 release gate. No network, no pulls, no pushes, no uploads, no training.

userStories.title: Modelfile generator from the frozen prompt (release_modelfile.py)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want every Ollama Modelfile generated from prompts/system_glb_v3.txt and one parameter set, so the :v1 and :v1-gguf tags cannot drift apart.
steps: Create scripts/release_modelfile.py: `--base NAME` (required, e.g. muse-glimmer:30b-mlx or muse-glimmer:30b), `--system FILE` (default prompts/system_glb_v3.txt), `--expect-sha256 HEX` (default the frozen v3 hash from docs/15 section 2), `--out FILE` (refused inside data/, out/, eval/ and release/v1/). It refuses when the system file's sha256 differs from the expected hash, naming both hashes.

Output format exactly: `FROM <base>`, blank line, `SYSTEM """` + the file's text + `"""`, blank line, then `PARAMETER temperature 0.7`, `PARAMETER top_p 0.95`, `PARAMETER num_ctx 49152`, `PARAMETER num_predict 40000`, one per line, trailing newline. Refuse a system file that contains a triple double quote.

Tests (tests/py/test_release_modelfile.py): generating with --base muse-glimmer:30b-mlx reproduces release/v1/Modelfile byte for byte; --base muse-glimmer:30b differs only in the FROM line; a wrong hash, a forbidden --out and a system text with a triple quote are each refused with a clear message.
acceptanceCriteria: Byte-identical reproduction of release/v1/Modelfile is asserted
Hash mismatch, forbidden output path and triple-quote cases are asserted
No file under release/v1/ is modified
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: Model rows for the released tags, with a no-system-message mode
userStories.description: As the owner, I want to benchmark the published Ollama tags exactly as a user calls them (no system message, the baked-in one applies), so the release numbers describe what users get.
steps: teacher_generate.py: add `--no-system`. With it, both the Ollama-native and the OpenAI-compatible routes send only the user message, and the raw row records `system_file: null` and `system_sha256: null`. Without it, behaviour is unchanged (assert the existing tests still pass).
glb_bench.py: a model row may set `"system": null`; it then passes --no-system and skips the system-file existence check. Other rows are unchanged.

bench/glb/models.json: add two rows, both `enabled: false`, `paid: false`, `think: false`, `system: null`, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95: `meshwright-v1` (model `khanzz_irfan/meshwright-glimmer-30b-lora:v1`) and `meshwright-v1-gguf` (model `khanzz_irfan/meshwright-glimmer-30b-lora:v1-gguf`). Do not change any existing row.

Tests: a fake Ollama HTTP server records the request body; with --no-system the messages list has exactly one user message; the bench builds the --no-system command for a null-system row; models.json loads and the glimmer-v3 row is byte-for-byte unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: The recorded request has no system message with --no-system and has one without it
Both new rows exist, disabled, and every existing row is unchanged
Existing teacher_generate and bench tests pass unchanged
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: Release preflight (release_check.py)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want one command that tells me whether the release files and the repo are safe and consistent before anything goes public.
steps: Create scripts/release_check.py with checks that each print PASS or FAIL plus a reason, and exit 1 when any FAIL. Inputs default to docs/15 paths: `--model-card release/v1/hf-model/README.md`, `--dataset-card release/v1/hf-dataset/README.md`, `--dataset-dir release/v1/hf-dataset`, `--system prompts/system_glb_v3.txt`, `--repo-root .`, `--eval-briefs bench/glb/briefs.jsonl`.

Card checks: the credit line from docs/15 section 1 appears verbatim in both cards; the model card names `khanzz_irfan/meshwright-glimmer-30b-lora:v1`, the HF dataset id and the GitHub URL from docs/15 section 1; the sha256 printed in the model card equals the system file's; the phrase 'Fine-tuned from' does not appear in a card unless `--allow-finetuned` is given; `license: apache-2.0` is in both front matters.

Dataset checks: train.jsonl and val.jsonl row counts equal the numbers stated in the dataset card's Splits table; every row's system message hashes to the frozen sha256; no row id or title matches an eval brief id or title; no row contains any pattern from a private-pattern list (`/Users/`, `/home/`, an email regex, `sk-`, `hf_`, `api_key`, `BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY`), with `--extra-pattern` repeatable.

Repo checks: run `git ls-files` (subprocess, read only) and FAIL on tracked `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `*.pem`, `id_*`, any file over 50 MB, and any tracked text file under 2 MB containing the private patterns, listing at most 20 hits with path:line. Skip binary files.

Tests (tests/py/test_release_check.py) build a temp repo (git init in a temp dir), temp cards and temp JSONL: a clean setup passes; each failure (missing credit, wrong sha, wrong count, eval leak, email in a row, tracked .env, 'Fine-tuned from' without the flag) fails with its reason.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean fixture passes and each listed failure is asserted to FAIL with its reason
Only read-only git commands are used (asserted by checking the subprocess calls)
Exit codes are 0 for all PASS and 1 for any FAIL
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: Owner-session ops for the v1-gguf gate (rel_ops.sh)
userStories.description: As the owner session, I want one script that builds the cross-platform tag locally and runs the docs/15 section 4 gate, so the result is recorded the same way every time. It never pushes.
steps: Create scripts/rel_ops.sh following scripts/imp_ops.sh (start/status/stop, background jobs, logs and pid files under runs/rel/jobs/, refuse to start when the v3 prompt hash differs). Jobs: `gguf-pull` (`ollama pull muse-glimmer:30b`), `gguf-create` (release_modelfile.py --base muse-glimmer:30b --out runs/rel/Modelfile.v1-gguf, then `ollama create khanzz_irfan/meshwright-glimmer-30b-lora:v1-gguf -f` it), `gguf-dev` (glb_bench on bench/glb/dev_briefs.jsonl for the rows meshwright-v1 and meshwright-v1-gguf, then validate, then write runs/rel/gguf_dev.md), and `gguf-all` (the three in order, stopping at the first failure).

runs/rel/gguf_dev.md: a table per row of valid n/12, assembled of valid, median seconds, and a final line `GATE: PASS` or `GATE: FAIL (<reason>)` using the docs/15 section 4 rule (valid >= 10/12 and assembled-of-valid within 15 points of meshwright-v1). Put the gate computation in a small Python helper with unit tests.
The script must not contain the word `push` in any executed command; `status` prints the push command for the owner to run by hand only when the gate line says PASS.

Tests: a fake `ollama` on PATH records its arguments; every job's arguments are asserted against the real argument parsers (as in tests/py/test_imp_ops_parsers.py); the gate helper is tested on PASS, low-valid FAIL and assembled-gap FAIL fixtures; a grep-style test asserts no executed `ollama push`.
acceptanceCriteria: Every job's command line parses with the real parsers (asserted)
Gate PASS and both FAIL reasons are asserted
No executed push command exists in the script (asserted)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: v2 pod runbook, dry run first (v2_pod.sh)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want the v2 training steps from docs/15 section 5 as one script that prints the plan by default and cannot spend money without explicit flags.
steps: Create scripts/v2_pod.sh with subcommands `plan` (default; prints every step as commands: create an A100 80 GB pod, upload runs/imp/distill_data and the scripts, 20-step smoke, run glb_phase2_estimate.py with the measured sec-per-step, full training, merge, quantise, download the adapter, the loss curve and the quantised build, stop and delete the pod), `smoke`, `train` and `teardown`.

`smoke`, `train` and `teardown` refuse to run unless both `--approve-spend` and `--max-usd N` are given, print the estimated cost from glb_phase2_estimate.py next to N, and refuse when the estimate exceeds N. Every pod command goes through a single `run_remote` function so tests can stub it.
Before any spend it checks that runs/imp/distill_data has train.jsonl and val.jsonl with no eval ids (reuse glb_distill_prep.py or release_check.py helpers, do not copy).

Tests: `plan` output contains each step in order and makes no external calls; spend subcommands without the flags, or with an estimate over the cap, exit non-zero before calling the stubbed runpodctl; a fake runpodctl on PATH records that teardown always runs after a failed train (trap).
acceptanceCriteria: plan makes no external calls (asserted with a fake runpodctl that fails if called)
Missing flags and an over-cap estimate are refused before any pod command (asserted)
Teardown runs after a failure (asserted)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: v1-versus-v2 release gate (release_compare.py)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want the docs/15 section 5 release rule computed from run directories, so v2 is published only when it measurably beats v1.
steps: Create scripts/release_compare.py `--v1 RUN_DIR --v2 RUN_DIR [--v1-ratings CSV --v2-ratings CSV] [--out FILE]`. Read validation.jsonl and assembly.jsonl the way glb_report.py does (import its helpers). Compute valid rate, assembled of all briefs and median seconds per run, and, when both rating CSVs are given, the share rated 2 (good).

Decision: PUBLISH when v2 valid >= v1 valid, v2 assembled >= v1 assembled + 10 points and (when ratings exist) v2 good >= v1 good; otherwise HOLD with every failed condition listed. Without ratings the line says `PUBLISH (pending blind rating)` instead of PUBLISH. Print a Markdown table and the decision line; --out writes the same.
Refuse when the two runs cover different brief id sets, naming the differences.
Tests with temp run dirs: PUBLISH, HOLD on validity, HOLD on assembled margin, HOLD on rating, pending-rating wording and the mismatched-briefs refusal.
acceptanceCriteria: All four decisions and the refusal are asserted
glb_report.py helpers are imported, not copied (asserted by import in the test or by grep)
Seconds per brief are reported but never change the decision (asserted)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Build and test with fixtures, temp dirs, fake HTTP servers and a fake `ollama`/`hf`/`runpodctl` on PATH where needed. Never call the real Ollama, Hugging Face, GitHub or RunPod; never run ollama pull/create/push, hf upload, git push or any pod command for real. Never read or write runs/, data/, out/ or eval/ except through temp-dir fixtures. Never edit prompts/, bench/glb/briefs.jsonl, bench/glb/eval_subjects.json or the published files under release/v1/ (read them only). Never commit.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.

universal: `bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names
chromium: Browser-driven tests run against the installed Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` is already done); if Chromium cannot launch, say so in `notes` instead of skipping silently

The v1-gguf pull, create and 12-brief dev gate are started by the owner session through scripts/rel_ops.sh, not by Ralph
Every ollama push, hf upload, repo visibility change and git push is done by the owner session after the owner says so
